source.title: An opportunity cost model of subjective effort and task performance.

confidence_rationale: Kurzban et al. is the canonical statement of the OPPORTUNITY-COST account of subjective effort -- which is exactly REE's existing MECH-320/ARC-068 opportunity-cost-of-time machinery. They argue the aversive phenomenology of effort is the felt output of cost/benefit computations over foregone alternative uses of limited executive systems, and they explicitly ARGUE AGAINST the physical-resource-DEPLETION account that is the mechanistic cousin of Q-080's 'over-exertion -> depletion -> harm-adjacent state.' So this both (a) supports the sufficiency of value-subtraction/opportunity-cost and (b) casts specific doubt on the depletion story harm-coupling would rest on -- double-weakening for the harm proposal. Confidence 0.66: strong on the ordinary-effort regime and on the anti-depletion argument, but it is a theoretical target article (much-debated), and it addresses subjective mental effort rather than the metabolic over-exertion REE's harm-coupling most naturally concerns.
failure_signatures: If subjective effort is the felt output of opportunity-cost computation (next-best foregone use of executive systems), then effort is FOREGONE VALUE, not harm -- and REE's existing ARC-068/MECH-320 opportunity-cost machinery already captures it, leaving no gap for a harm channel to fill.

Kurzban et al. marshal evidence AGAINST resource-depletion accounts of effort (e.g. fatigue dissipates on task-switch, is sensitive to incentives). If REE's over-exertion state behaves like opportunity cost (incentive-sensitive, relieved by better alternatives) rather than like damage (persistent, irreversibility-flagged), the harm-coupling is falsified in favour of value-subtraction.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The aversive experience of mental effort, and the performance decrements that accompany sustained tasks, are not caused by depletion of a physical resource. Instead, executive/computational mechanisms can serve only a limited number of simultaneous tasks, so deploying them on the current task carries an OPPORTUNITY COST -- the next-best foregone use of those systems. The phenomenology of effort is the felt output of these cost/benefit computations, and it motivates disengagement (reduced deployment) from the current task. The authors review and reject resource-depletion explanations in favour of this opportunity-cost account.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-080 weighs harm-coupling of effort against sufficiency of value-subtraction, and it names MECH-320/ARC-068 opportunity-cost-of-time as the existing machinery. Kurzban et al. is the source theory for exactly that machinery. It frames wasted/excess effort as FOREGONE VALUE (opportunity cost), not as harm, directly supporting the 'value-subtraction suffices' pole. It goes further and attacks the physical-DEPLETION account -- and depletion is the mechanistic backbone of Q-080's 'over-exertion -> depletion -> harm-adjacent state.' So it weakens the harm proposal on two fronts: it offers a complete non-harm account, and it undermines the depletion premise harm-coupling would need.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Kurzban et al. concerns SUBJECTIVE MENTAL effort and executive-system time-sharing, whereas Q-080's harm-coupling is most naturally about METABOLIC/physical over-exertion and allostatic depletion. The anti-depletion argument is aimed at mental fatigue; it does not directly rule out genuine metabolic depletion from sustained physical exertion, which could still warrant harm-adjacent treatment. It is also a BBS target article -- deliberately provocative and extensively contested in the same issue (several commentaries defend depletion or resource views). So this weakens harm-coupling for the cognitive-effort regime while leaving the physical-exertion regime open.
mapping.source_context: Behavioral and Brain Sciences target article (2013), a theoretical synthesis with open peer commentary. Domain: human psychology / neuroeconomics of cognitive effort. No new primary data; argues from a broad review across psychology and neuroscience.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high -- a landmark, agenda-setting target article and the provenance of REE's opportunity-cost framing. Mapping fidelity good for the cognitive-effort regime and for the anti-depletion argument. Transfer risk moderate: the mental-effort vs metabolic-over-exertion regime gap (in the caveat) and the fact that the target article's depletion critique is itself contested keep this from being a strong weakens.
